# Handoff §9.5's particle-absorbing merge class: jparser absorbing a preceding
# particle or fragment into the following word and matching a kana-unified
# headword that is semantically absurd. Vibrato has the boundary in every one.
#
# Regenerated from examples/boundary_diag.rs over tests/fixtures/gold.jsonl and
# tests/fixtures/gold_jmdict_subset.xml (the committed gold corpus and its
# v1 index), against corpus_staging/disagreements.jsonl -- a local, gitignored
# Phase 0 measurement artifact already present in this environment and
# byte-identical in its gold half to the committed corpus. That run reproduces
# handoff §9's headline table exactly (266 boundaries, 178/52/36 by stage,
# 92 in the "ordinary longer headword" kind). This project's own §9.5 sample
# listed ten rows out of "roughly 28" from that 92-row bucket without
# enumerating the rest; the remaining rows below were hand-classified against
# that same 92-row bucket for this task, cross-checked against each matched
# ent_seq's actual JMdict gloss (via tests/fixtures/gold_jmdict_subset.xml)
# and, where the gloss alone did not settle it, against the exact gold-span
# boundaries of the originating sentence in tests/fixtures/gold.jsonl. Two
# variant surfaces of an already-documented ent_seq (a different exact text
# hitting the same spurious match) are included alongside it. Three katakana
# homophone-collision rows (クで/タは/ヌの) and one differently-shaped row
# (的で, from 目的 mis-split) that handoff §9.5 also names are excluded here:
# they do not fit the surface/ent_seq/split shape this file uses, matching
# this task's brief, which already excludes them from its own template.
#
# The accounting is not closed. 26 rows here + the 3 excluded katakana rows +
# the 1 excluded 目的 row = 30, past the source document's own "roughly 28" --
# and a first pass at this file (task 15) missed タッとい/1598620 (added on
# review) among the 92, so the 92-row bucket may still hold rows this pass
# also missed. Treat 26 as a lower bound on the class within this file's
# shape, not a closed count.
#
# The third column is documentation, not a literal reconstruction of the
# surface: it is not checked by the test, and for some rows (はこ, どうし,
# ことし, いっしょ) it names wider sentence context or a lemma form that does
# not fit the surface's own character count. See the Phase 1a handoff
# (`docs/superpowers/2026-09-01-engine-v2-phase1a-handoff.md`) §5 and §8 on
# why the third column is documentation rather than an assertion.
#
# THE FOURTH COLUMN IS CHECKED. It names a `source` in
# tests/fixtures/gold.jsonl: a committed, adjudicated sentence that contains
# the surface AND whose gold segmentation puts a boundary strictly inside it,
# so the corpus itself asserts that the surface must not be one word there.
# All 26 rows have one; none of the sentences is invented for this test.
#
# It was added because testing the surface in isolation could not measure what
# this file is about. Given only a bare two-character string, Vibrato treats
# はこ, うん and んで as one token each, so `cost.rs`'s crossing count -- which
# looks strictly *between* a span's endpoints -- finds no interior boundary and
# neither CROSS nor PRONOUNCE_CROSS can fire at any magnitude. Three of the
# four rows that failed before this column existed failed for that reason and
# not for an engine one; the fourth (いんじゃない) failed because じゃ is
# missing from the small curated tests/fixtures/jmdict_subset.xml, which is why
# the test now builds from gold_jmdict_subset.xml, where じゃ is one of four
# real JMdict entries.
#
# Nothing here is captured text or ported expression: these are ordinary
# Japanese strings this project measured about its own engine.
#
# surface	ent_seq	what it actually is	gold sentence asserting the split
はいた	1399760	は + いた	d:a:003521-6
はこう	1399760	は + こう	a:004842-3
ももう	1567610	も + もう	a:004601-8
はこ	1585650	は + この	b:wn3065-1
がい	1204330	が + いった	a:053148-4
になって	1599900	に + なる	b:wn28412-1
になった	1599900	に + なった	a:004601-8
# してい no longer has a cut inside it, and the row is kept and still
# asserting (2026-09-18). ている joined table.rs's ATTACHES_TO, so
# 予定にしている reads 予定 | に | している: the に is its own span, nothing is
# absorbed, and the covering segment's top entry is する Progressive rather
# than 1308000 (指定) or the kana-unified 子弟/師弟 this row exists for. The
# test's acceptance was widened to match the row's subject instead of a
# proxy for it: a strictly longer matched word covering the surface passes
# **only when its top entry is not this column-2 ent_seq**, and a segment
# sitting exactly on the surface still fails whatever it matched. Verified
# before the change: across eight readings of that sentence 指定 never takes
# the span, and してい parsed alone now leads with する Progressive where it
# used to lead with 子弟 "children; sons".
してい	1308000	して + いた	b:wn25517-3
どうし	1451380	どう + しました	d:a:000323-3
